{{Top}}
[[File:MTD-FF83.png|thumb|right|300px|[[M-TD]]'s grated vocabulator was located between his [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]].]]
{{Quote|You sound strange. Is something wrong with your vocabulator?|A BX-series droid commando to Clone Captain "Rex" while the captain was pretending to be a commando droid|audio=Vocabulator-Rookies.flac|<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref>}}
A '''vocabulator''', also known as a '''vocoder''', was a speech synthesizer that was fitted to almost all types of [[Droid/Legends|droids]] that were intended to interact with [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings. Some droids, such as [[HK-series assassin droid]]s and [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]]&mdash;which were commonly fluent in many [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] languages&mdash;could use their vocabulators to mimic or impersonate the voices of other beings or creatures.

The [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|Tranlang III Vocabulator]] was one such model that was used in the [[3PO-series protocol droid]], granting models of this line the ability to articulate in over six million forms of communication. This model of vocoder also saw use in governmental droids.

Droids lacking a vocabulator could resort to external translator units.<ref name="BL">{{GamerCite|7|Bartyn's Landing (article)}}</ref>

Vocoders could also be fitted as [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] attachments for organic beings that had suffered injuries that cost them their ability to speak. [[Darth Malak]] was equipped with a vocoder attachment that served to replace his severed jaw, as was [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] almost 4,000 years later. In Vader's case, the vocoder served to enhance what little speaking ability he had left after his vocal cords were scorched on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]]. [[Wat Tambor]] also used such a device, although he was shown to have to frequently adjust it using attachments on his metal suit as one would tune a [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|radio]].

A [[transliterator]] was a similar device. It translated speech into another programmed voice.

{{Tech-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
There is a real-world electronic device called a [[Wikipedia:Vocoder|vocoder]] with communication and musical uses. This bears no resemblance to the ''Star Wars'' device.

''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' spells the device "vocodor."
